start:
CONSULT · GET A SECOND OPINION

Start a new topic:
  /consult ask Should we choose Vendor A or Vendor B?

Ask the panel a follow-up on your selected topic:
  /consult more What if my budget is smaller?

Original model answers:
  /consult sources

Switch topics:
  /consult topics
  /consult use 2

Finish and clear your selection:
  /consult done

Messages without /consult stay normal chat with your agent. They do not ask other models.

Consult automatically chooses distinct models using their configured settings. You get a combined answer; original replies remain available separately. More asks the panel again. To explain existing answers locally, use /consult lens contrast (this still uses your agent's model).

No topic name, ID, or flags are needed for the basic flow. In group chats, each participant has their own topic selection. Topic numbers refer to your most recent /consult topics list.

More help: /consult help topics, /consult help continue, or /consult help all.
references:
REFERENCES · ROOT, TAG, NODE, AND ACTIVE ROOT

REF = ROOT, TAG, or NODE.

  ROOT  C007                 permanent id for the whole topic
  TAG   atlas-switch         friendly alias for the same topic
  NODE  C007:A1              one exact node in the topic graph
  NODE  atlas-switch:A1      the same node addressed through its tag

ROOT and TAG both mean “start from this topic's original question.” A NODE means “anchor to this exact question, answer, critique, synthesis, or judgment.”

Starting, explicitly continuing, /consult use, and reopening select the topic for the caller. Inspection does not change that selection. Closing or deleting clears selections pointing at that topic; it never silently selects a different topic.

Choose it explicitly:
  /consult use atlas-switch

When syntax shows [REF], omitting it uses the active root. Commands that contain a free-text question—continue and branch—require REF explicitly so Consult can distinguish the reference from the question.

Find references:
  /consult recent
  /consult roots
  /consult roots --closed
  /consult show atlas-switch --view graph

For everyday follow-ups, /consult more QUESTION uses your selected topic without a reference. --tag is used only when starting a new consultation; use the tag directly afterward. Unicode mobile dash options (for example —tag) are accepted. Untagged topics receive a readable title from the question and a stable internal alias.
protocols:
PROTOCOLS · HOW THE PANEL APPROACHES THE QUESTION

METHOD     TARGETS  DEFAULT LOCAL LENS  PURPOSE
quick      up to 2  distill             fast independent comparison
deep       up to 3  distill             broader, fuller comparison
verify     up to 3  critique            check facts, assumptions, omissions
decide     up to 3  referee             recommend an action
explore    up to 3  extend              find implications and alternatives
debate     up to 2  contrast            expose concrete disagreements
redteam    up to 2  critique            search for failure modes
forecast   up to 3  referee             compare predictions and signposts

Syntax:
  /consult METHOD [--tag TAG] [--to auto|a,b] [--lens LENS] [--tier agent=LEVEL] QUESTION
  /consult LENS [--tag TAG] [--to auto|a,b] [--tier agent=LEVEL] QUESTION

Examples:
  /consult verify --tag rollout-risk Is this rollout plan safe?
  /consult decide --tag vendor-choice --lens counsel Which vendor should we use?

METHOD controls panel size and intent. --lens optionally replaces only the local processing style described in /consult help lenses.

The second form is a convenience shortcut: a lens name in the command position
starts a new consultation with the profile's default method and that lens.
For example, /consult distill ... means method quick + lens distill by default.

Use the profile's default method (quick unless changed):
  /consult ask [--tag TAG] [--to auto|a,b] [--lens LENS] [--tier agent=LEVEL] QUESTION

Web presets: Second opinion = quick + distill; Check reasoning = verify + critique; Help me decide = decide + referee. Check reasoning compares model reasoning; agreement does not prove a fact. Options expose all methods and lenses. Protocols describe independent panel intent; debate is not an automatic multi-round exchange.

Examples for all methods:
/consult quick Compare these options.
/consult deep Compare these options.
/consult verify Compare these options.
/consult decide Compare these options.
/consult explore Compare these options.
/consult debate Compare these options.
/consult redteam Compare these options.
/consult forecast Compare these options.
lenses:
LENSES · HOW THIS AGENT PROCESSES STORED ANSWERS

LENS       RESULT
distill    integrate sources into one answer, preserving gaps/disagreements
critique   identify errors, weak reasoning, assumptions, and omissions
counsel    advise: what resonates, what to question, what else matters
steelman   strengthen each position before judging it
extend     add implications, changed assumptions, and unstated ideas
contrast   explain concrete disagreements without forcing a synthesis
referee    weigh support, uncertainty, and give a recommendation

There are three deliberately different lens forms:

1. /consult LENS ... starts a new consultation, contacts external agents, and
uses the profile's default panel method with that lens:
  /consult distill --tag health-question What could explain this pain?
  /consult critique --tag rollout-risk Is this rollout safe?

2. --lens LENS is an option on a method, continue, or branch. It chooses the automatic local processing after the new external replies arrive:
  /consult quick --tag pricing --lens critique Is this pricing plan sound?
  /consult continue pricing --lens counsel What should we do next?

3. /consult lens [REF] LENS reprocesses answers already stored in the graph. It does not contact external agents, although the invoking container's current model performs the new processing:
  /consult lens pricing steelman
  /consult lens pricing:A1 critique
  /consult lens referee              uses the active root

Shortcuts over existing stored sources:
  /consult judge [REF]       same as lens REF referee
  /consult challenge [REF]   same as lens REF critique
  /consult revise [REF]      same as lens REF distill

Start a new topic using a specific answer style:
/consult distill Compare these options.
/consult critique Compare these options.
/consult counsel Compare these options.
/consult steelman Compare these options.
/consult extend Compare these options.
/consult contrast Compare these options.
/consult referee Compare these options.
models:
MODELS · ROSTER, TARGETS, AND OVERRIDES

Inspect or refresh this session's cached model roster:
  /consult roster
  /consult roster --refresh

Target selection:
  /consult quick --tag architecture --to auto QUESTION
  /consult quick --tag architecture --to atlas,errand-runner QUESTION

Default rule: every target uses its current configured model, tier, effort, provider, and harness unchanged. Automatic selection skips targets whose effective model duplicates the invoking model or an already selected target.

The only model override is an explicit per-target tier inside the user's command:
  /consult quick --to atlas --tier atlas=high QUESTION
  /consult deep --to atlas,errand-runner --tier atlas=high,errand-runner=low QUESTION

LEVEL is high, medium, or low and must exist in that target's roster receipt. Consult never upgrades or switches a model implicitly.
continue:
FOLLOW UP · ASK THE PANEL AGAIN

Everyday syntax:
  /consult more What changes if cost doubles?

More uses your selected topic and its bounded completed history. Its reply names that topic. If none is selected, Consult asks you to start or select one; it never guesses from normal chat.

Use /consult sources for original model replies. Use /consult lens contrast to explain existing answers locally without asking the panel again.

Advanced controls:

CONTINUE OR BRANCH · SEND A NEW QUESTION

Canonical syntax:
  /consult continue REF [--protocol METHOD] [--to auto|a,b] [--lens LENS] [--tier agent=LEVEL] QUESTION
  /consult branch   REF [--protocol METHOD] [--to auto|a,b] [--lens LENS] [--tier agent=LEVEL] QUESTION

continue adds a follow-up edge. branch records an explicit alternative line of inquiry. Both send a new question to distinct external models and automatically process the replies.

Anchor rules:
  /consult continue vendor-choice What changes if cost doubles?
    TAG anchors to the topic's original question.

  /consult continue vendor-choice:A2 Which assumption supports that claim?
    NODE anchors to that exact answer.

  /consult branch C007:S1 Explore the opposite recommendation
    NODE creates a branch from that synthesis.

REF is required here because the rest of the command is free-text QUESTION. Even when a topic is active, continue and branch require REF. --tag is not valid: it creates names only for new roots. --protocol and --lens affect only this new question; they do not rename or rewrite the root's defaults.
inspect:
INSPECT · GRAPH, SOURCES, AND EXACT TEXT

Topic summaries (omitting REF uses the active root):
  /consult show [ROOT|TAG] --view compact
  /consult show [ROOT|TAG] --view graph
  /consult show [ROOT|TAG] --view full
  /consult show [ROOT|TAG] --view sources

Source overview:
  /consult sources [ROOT|TAG]

One exact content node:
  /consult raw NODE

Examples:
  /consult show vendor-choice --view graph
  /consult sources vendor-choice
  /consult raw vendor-choice:A1

raw shows short content inline and sends long content as a text attachment. Exact remote answers and this agent's later processed outputs remain separate files with hashes and execution receipts.
lifecycle:
TOPICS · SELECT AND FINISH

/consult topics          show a numbered topic list
/consult use NUMBER      select from your most recent list
/consult more QUESTION   follow up on your selected topic
/consult done            close that topic and clear its selection

Numbers stay tied to the list you saw, even if a new topic is created. Run /consult topics again to refresh the list. You can also use /consult use ROOT|TAG.

Starting, explicitly continuing, selecting, or reopening a topic selects it for you. Another participant does not change your selection. Closing or deleting a topic clears selections pointing at it; no other topic is silently selected.

A closed topic can be inspected. To ask the panel again, select it, then use the /consult reopen command shown in the response. Closed topics follow bounded retention; they are not a permanent archive.

The selected topic is local to this conversation session. Ordinary chat never implicitly contacts the panel.

LIFECYCLE · ACTIVE, CLOSED, AND TRASHED ROOTS

Select the active root:
  /consult use ROOT|TAG

List roots:
  /consult recent
  /consult roots
  /consult roots --closed

Close without deleting (omitting REF uses the active root):
  /consult close [ROOT|TAG]

Recover or remove:
  /consult reopen ROOT|TAG
  /consult delete [ROOT|TAG]
  /consult restore ROOT|TAG

Defaults are bounded: 3 open/recent roots; 20 closed roots for up to 30 days; 10 trashed roots for up to 7 days; 64 MiB total. A fourth open root auto-closes the oldest. Quota pruning removes trash and closed roots first and never silently destroys an open root.

Inspect local settings:
  /consult profile show
examples:
EXAMPLES · WHATSAPP RECIPES

/consult ask Which vendor should we choose?
/consult more What changes if cost doubles?
/consult sources
/consult lens contrast
/consult done

Return later:
/consult topics
/consult use 1
Then send the reopen command shown if the topic is closed.

Advanced examples:

EXAMPLES · COMPLETE WORKFLOWS

1. Start and keep a memorable tag:
  /consult decide --tag vendor-choice Which vendor should we choose and why?

2. Alternatively, start by naming the desired processing lens directly:
  /consult distill --tag vendor-choice Which vendor should we choose and why?

3. Inspect the returned graph:
  /consult show vendor-choice --view graph

4. Ask models a follow-up anchored to one exact answer:
  /consult continue vendor-choice:A1 --lens critique Challenge its migration-cost assumption

5. Reprocess stored answers locally without contacting agents again:
  /consult lens vendor-choice steelman

6. Read source text rather than the local synthesis:
  /consult sources vendor-choice
  /consult raw vendor-choice:A1

7. Continue ordinary conversation with the current agent simply by not using /consult.

8. Finish the topic without losing it:
  /consult close vendor-choice

9. Remove it recoverably:
  /consult delete vendor-choice
  /consult restore vendor-choice

profile:
PROFILE · SETTINGS

/consult profile show
/consult profile set KEY VALUE

Keys: defaultProtocol, defaultLens, recentLimit, closedLimit, closedDays, trashLimit, trashDays, maxBytes.

Examples:
/consult profile set defaultProtocol quick
/consult profile set recentLimit 5

Settings apply to this conversation session. Existing topics and original answers are preserved. Starts normally use the method's answer style unless an explicit lens is supplied; the defaultLens key does not override a method's built-in style.
